points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 1632年8月29日，约翰·洛克出生于英国萨默塞特郡的灵顿一个富裕的清教徒家庭。父亲是小土地所有者和律师，在英国内战时期担任过议会军的军官。洛克在家庭接受了良好的基础教育，展现出对古典文学和哲学的早期兴趣。这段时期的教育为他后来的思想发展奠定了基础，特别是他对宗教宽容和个人自由的早期思考。
points.descriptionEn: John Locke was born on August 29, 1632, in Wrington, Somerset, England, to a wealthy Puritan family. His father was a small landowner and lawyer who served as an officer in Parliament's army during the English Civil War. Locke received a solid education at home, showing early interest in classical literature and philosophy. This formative period laid the foundation for his later intellectual development, particularly his early thoughts on religious tolerance and individual freedom.

points.title: 学术奠基
points.description: 1652年，洛克进入牛津大学基督教堂学院学习，主要专注于古典学、哲学和医学。在牛津期间，他深受笛卡尔和罗伯特·波义耳等新思想家的影响，对经验主义哲学产生了浓厚兴趣。1656年获得学士学位，1658年获得硕士学位。这段时期他开始质疑传统的经院哲学，并开始发展自己的经验主义认识论，同时掌握了医学知识，这为他后来与罗伯特·波义耳等科学家的交往奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1652, Locke entered Christ Church College, Oxford, where he studied classics, philosophy, and medicine. During his time at Oxford, he was deeply influenced by new thinkers like René Descartes and Robert Boyle, developing a keen interest in empiricist philosophy. He received his bachelor's degree in 1656 and master's degree in 1658. This period saw him begin to question traditional scholastic philosophy and develop his own empiricist epistemology, while also acquiring medical knowledge that would later facilitate his relationships with scientists like Robert Boyle.

points.title: 从政生涯
points.description: 1667年，洛克通过医学知识结识了安东尼·阿什利·库珀（后来的沙夫茨伯里伯爵），成为其私人医生和政治顾问。在伦敦期间，洛克积极参与政治活动，撰写了大量政治论文，支持议会权力和王室限制。1670年，他开始撰写《政府论》（下篇），但直到1689年才出版。1675年，因沙夫茨伯里伯爵失势，洛克被迫离开英国前往法国，这段政治经历深刻影响了洛克的政治思想，特别是他对权力制衡和政府合法性的思考。
points.descriptionEn: In 1667, Locke met Anthony Ashley Cooper (later Earl of Shaftesbury) through his medical knowledge and became his private physician and political advisor. During his time in London, Locke actively participated in politics, writing numerous political essays supporting parliamentary power and limitations on the monarchy. He began writing his 'Two Treatises of Government' in 1670, though it wasn't published until 1689. In 1675, following Shaftesbury's political downfall, Locke was forced to leave England for France. This political experience profoundly influenced Locke's political thought, particularly his ideas about checks and balances and the legitimacy of government.

points.title: 法国流亡
points.description: 1675年至1679年，洛克在法国度过流亡生活，主要在蒙彼利埃和巴黎。在法国期间，他深入研究了笛卡尔哲学和法国科学家的思想，同时继续完善自己的政治理论。他结识了许多法国知识分子，包括皮埃尔·伽桑狄，其思想对洛克产生了重要影响。这段时期洛克完成了《人类理解论》的初稿，并开始系统阐述他的经验主义认识论。法国的流亡经历使洛克的思想更加成熟，也为他后来回到英国参与政治变革做好了准备。
points.descriptionEn: From 1675 to 1679, Locke lived in exile in France, primarily in Montpellier and Paris. During this time, he studied Cartesian philosophy and the ideas of French scientists in depth, while continuing to develop his political theories. He met many French intellectuals, including Pierre Gassendi, whose ideas significantly influenced him. This period saw Locke complete the first draft of his 'Essay Concerning Human Understanding' and systematically articulate his empiricist epistemology. His French exile experience matured his thinking and prepared him for his later return to England to participate in political changes.

points.title: 思想成熟
points.description: 1689年，洛克随光荣革命返回英国，被任命为贸易和殖民事务委员会的专员。这一时期是他创作的黄金期，出版了《政府论》（上下篇）、《人类理解论》和《论宗教宽容》等重要著作。1690年代，洛克逐渐退出政治舞台，专注于哲学和教育工作。他在埃塞克斯郡的家中接待了许多知识分子，传播他的思想。洛克的这些著作对启蒙运动产生了深远影响，成为美国独立宣言和法国大革命的思想源泉。1704年10月28日，洛克在埃塞克斯郡去世，享年72岁，留下了影响世界政治哲学的宝贵遗产。
points.descriptionEn: In 1689, Locke returned to England with the Glorious Revolution and was appointed Commissioner of Trade and Plantations. This period marked his golden age of publication, with major works including 'Two Treatises of Government', 'Essay Concerning Human Understanding', and 'A Letter Concerning Toleration'. During the 1690s, Locke gradually withdrew from politics to focus on philosophy and education. He hosted many intellectuals at his home in Essex, disseminating his ideas. Locke's works profoundly influenced the Enlightenment and became intellectual sources for the American Declaration of Independence and the French Revolution. On October 28, 1704, Locke died in Essex at the age of 72, leaving a legacy that profoundly shaped world political philosophy.

appraisal.zh: 洛克被公认为现代自由主义之父与启蒙运动的核心人物，其自然权利、社会契约、分权与宗教宽容诸说为民主制度奠定了理论基础，直接影响了美国《独立宣言》与宪法的制定，经验主义认识论亦开辟了现代哲学的新方向，"生命、自由和财产"至今被广泛引用。也有研究者指出，他的财产权理论客观上为资本主义与殖民扩张辩护，对妇女与下层阶级的权利论述不足，其支持奴隶制的立场更与自然权利学说自相矛盾。这些局限虽已被历史超越，却提醒人们其自由主义带有明显的精英色彩。
appraisal.en: Locke is recognized as the father of modern liberalism and a central figure of the Enlightenment: his ideas of natural rights, social contract, separation of powers and religious tolerance laid the theoretical groundwork for democratic institutions and directly shaped the American Declaration of Independence and Constitution, while his empiricism opened a new direction in modern philosophy, and 'life, liberty, and property' is still widely quoted. Yet researchers also note that his theory of property in effect justified capitalism and colonial expansion, that his treatment of rights for women and the lower classes was inadequate, and that his support for slavery contradicted his own natural-rights doctrine. These limits have been superseded by history, but they mark his liberalism as distinctly elitist.

supporter.zh: 洛克被誉为现代自由主义之父，他的思想为民主社会奠定了理论基础。支持者认为他提出的自然权利、社会契约、三权分立和宗教宽容等理念，是人类政治文明的重大进步。洛克强调个人自由、财产权和有限政府，这些思想直接影响了美国独立宣言和宪法的制定。他的经验主义认识论也开创了现代哲学的新方向，强调知识来源于感官经验，而非天赋观念。
supporter.en: Locke is hailed as the father of modern liberalism, whose ideas laid the theoretical foundation for democratic societies. Supporters argue that his concepts of natural rights, social contract, separation of powers, and religious tolerance represent significant advancements in political civilization. Locke's emphasis on individual liberty, property rights, and limited government directly influenced the American Declaration of Independence and Constitution. His empiricist epistemology also pioneered a new direction in modern philosophy, emphasizing that knowledge derives from sensory experience rather than innate ideas.

critic.zh: 批评者指出洛克的思想存在明显的局限性。他的财产权理论被批评为为资本主义和殖民扩张提供了理论辩护，忽视了原住民土地权。洛克对妇女和下层阶级的权利论述不足，其自由主义本质上是一种精英自由主义。此外，洛克支持奴隶制的立场与其自然权利理论自相矛盾，反映了当时社会的种族偏见。他的经验主义也被认为过于简化了人类认知的复杂性，忽视了理性在知识形成中的重要作用。
critic.en: Critics point out significant limitations in Locke's thought. His theory of property rights has been criticized for providing theoretical justification for capitalism and colonial expansion while ignoring indigenous land rights. Locke's discussions of rights for women and lower classes were inadequate, making his liberalism essentially an elitist doctrine. Furthermore, his support for slavery contradicted his natural rights theory, reflecting the racial prejudices of his time. His empiricism has also been seen as oversimplifying the complexity of human cognition, underestimating the role of reason in knowledge formation.

objective.zh: 从历史和流行文化视角看，洛克被公认为启蒙运动的核心人物之一，其思想跨越时空影响深远。在学术界，他被视为连接英国经验主义与大陆理性主义的桥梁，其政治哲学成为现代民主制度的理论基石。在流行文化中，洛克的肖像经常出现在与自由、民主相关的艺术作品中，他的名言'生命、自由和财产'被广泛引用。尽管他的某些观点已被历史超越，但他关于政府权力应受限制、个人权利应受保护的核心思想，至今仍是现代政治文明的重要支柱。
objective.en: From historical and cultural perspectives, Locke is widely recognized as one of the central figures of the Enlightenment, whose ideas have had far-reaching influence across time and space. Academically, he is seen as a bridge between British empiricism and continental rationalism, with his political philosophy forming the theoretical foundation of modern democratic systems. In popular culture, Locke's portrait frequently appears in artworks related to freedom and democracy, and his maxim 'life, liberty, and property' is widely quoted. While some of his views have been superseded by history, his core ideas about limited government power and protected individual rights remain important pillars of modern political civilization.

self.zh: 政府的目的在于保护人们的生命、自由和财产权，当政府违背这一目的时，人民有权改变或废除它。
self.en: The end of law is not to abolish or restrain, but to preserve and enlarge freedom. For in all the states of created beings capable of law, where there is no law, there is no freedom.
